description: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts for two categories—“Open” and “Cons.”—across four essay genres: Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository, as part of the EssayBench evaluation framework for large language models in multi-genre Chinese essay writing. The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 130 in increments of 20, while the horizontal axis lists the four genres in left-to-right order. For each genre, two adjacent bars represent the sample counts: light blue for “Open” and light pink for “Cons.” In the Argumentative genre, “Open” has 79 samples and “Cons.” has 122; in Narrative, “Open” has 80 and “Cons.” has 87; in Descriptive, “Open” has 68 and “Cons.” has 103 (with a small gray bar segment above the pink bar indicating an additional 3 samples, bringing the total to 103); and in Expository, “Open” has 62 and “Cons.” has 130. The “Cons.” category consistently has higher sample counts than “Open” across all genres, with the largest gap observed in the Expository genre. The chart uses a simple grouped bar layout with numerical labels on top of each bar for precise values, and a legend in the upper right corner identifies the color coding for the two categories.
